arxiv-1801-10171.title: Null Infinity and Unitary Representation of The Poincare Group
arxiv-1801-10171.creator: Shamik Banerjee
arxiv-1801-10171.description: Abstract Following Pasterski-Shao-Strominger we construct a new basis of states in the single-particle Hilbert space of massless particles as a linear combination of standard Wigner states. Under Lorentz transformation the new basis states transform in the Unitary Principal Continuous Series representation.

arxiv-2201-08476.title: Search for resonances decaying to three \PW bosons in proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2201-08476.description: Abstract A search for resonances decaying into a \PW boson and a radion, where the radion decays into two \PW bosons, is presented. The data analyzed correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 \fbinv recorded in proton-proton collisions with the CMS detector at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV .

arxiv-2209-12109.title: Electronic and magnetic properties of the topological semimetal SmMg 2 Bi 2
arxiv-2209-12109.creator: Asish K. Kundu, Santanu Pakhira, Tufan Roy, T. Yilmaz, Masahito Tsujikawa, Masafumi Shirai, E. Vescovo, D. C. Johnston, Abhay N. Pasupathy, Tonica Valla
arxiv-2209-12109.description: Abstract Dirac semimetals show nontrivial physical properties and can host exotic quantum states like Weyl semimetals and topological insulators under suitable external conditions. Here, by combining angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy measurements (ARPES) and first-principle calculations, we demonstrate that the Zintl-phase compound SmMg 2 Bi 2 is in close proximity to a topological Dirac semimetallic state.

arxiv-2209-13601.title: Evaporation before disruption: comparing timescales for Jovian planets in star-forming regions 2022 Evaporation before disruption: comparing timescales for Jovian planets in star-forming regions – References
arxiv-2209-13601.creator: Emma C. Daffern-Powell, Richard J. Parker
arxiv-2209-13601.description: Abstract Simulations show that the orbits of planets are readily disrupted in dense star-forming regions; planets can be exchanged between stars, become free-floating and then be captured by other stars. However, dense star-forming regions also tend to be populous, containing massive stars that emit photoionising radiation, which can evaporate the gas in protoplanetary discs.

arxiv-2303-12555.title: A convenient inclusion of inhomogeneous boundary conditions in minimal residual methods Thanks: This research has been supported by the NSF Grant DMS ID 1720297.
arxiv-2303-12555.creator: Rob Stevenson
arxiv-2303-12555.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Rob Stevenson. Inhomogeneous essential boundary conditions can be appended to a well-posed PDE to lead to a combined variational formulation. The domain of the corresponding operator is a Sobolev space on the domain Ω \Omega on which the PDE is posed, whereas the codomain is a Cartesian product of spaces, among them fractional Sobolev spaces of functions on ∂ Ω \partial\Omega .

arxiv-2306-10992.title: Wellposedness of Boussinesq system
arxiv-2306-10992.description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider the viscous, incompressible, nonlinear Boussinesq system in two and three spatial dimension. We study the existence and regularity of solutions to the Boussinesq system with nonhomogeneous boundary conditions for which the normal component for the velocity is not necessary equal to zero.

arxiv-2312-08767.title: FR0 jets and recollimation-induced instabilities
arxiv-2312-08767.creator: A. Costa, G. Bodo, F. Tavecchio, P. Rossi, A. Capetti, S. Massaglia, A. Sciaccaluga, R. D. Baldi, G. Giovannini
arxiv-2312-08767.description: Abstract Context. The recently discovered population of faint FR0 radiogalaxies has been interpreted as the extension to low power of the classical FRI sources. Their radio emission appears to be concentrated in very compact (pc-scale) cores, any extended emission is very weak or absent and VLBI observations show that jets are already mildly or sub-relativistic at pc scales.

arxiv-2409-18989.title: SC-Phi2: A Fine-tuned Small Language Model for StarCraft II Macromanagement Tasks
arxiv-2409-18989.creator: Muhammad Junaid Khan, Gita Sukthankar
arxiv-2409-18989.description: Abstract This paper introduces SC-Phi2, a fine-tuned StarCraft II small language model for macromanagement tasks. Small language models, like Phi2, Gemma, and DistilBERT, are streamlined versions of large language models (LLMs) with fewer parameters that require less power and memory to run.

arxiv-2505-20028.title: Capillary wave formation in conserved active emulsions
arxiv-2505-20028.creator: Florian Raßhofer, Simon Bauer, Alexander Ziepke, Ivan Maryshev, Erwin Frey
arxiv-2505-20028.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Florian Raßhofer, Simon Bauer, Alexander Ziepke, Ivan Maryshev, Erwin Frey. The dynamics of phase-separated interfaces shape the behavior of both passive and active condensates. While surface tension in equilibrium systems minimizes interface length, non-equilibrium fluxes can destabilize flat or constantly curved interfaces, giving rise to complex interface morphologies. Starting from a minimal model that couples a conserved, phase-separating species to a self-generated chemical field, we identify the conditions under which interfacial instabilities may emerge.

arxiv-2506-18972.title: The Relationship of Stellar Radius Inflation to Rotation and Magnetic Starspots at 10–670 Myr Journal: ApJL
arxiv-2506-18972.creator: Lyra Cao, Keivan G. Stassun
arxiv-2506-18972.description: Abstract Active, low-mass stars are widely observed to have radii that are larger than predicted by standard stellar models. Proposed mechanisms for this radius inflation generally involve stellar magnetism, either in the form of added pressure support in the outer layers and/or suppression of convection via starspots.

pmc-10572055.title: Effect of Sarcopenia on Pneumonia after Endoscopic Submucosal Resection in Patients Aged ≥65 Years: A Retrospective Study
pmc-10572055.creator: Min-Yu Kim, So Yeon Kim, Hye Jung Shin, Ki Hong Kweon, Jooeun Park, Na Young Kim, Tateaki Naito
pmc-10572055.description: Simple SummaryElderly patients have a higher risk of developing pneumonia due to a decrease in the swallowing function and the effectiveness of coughing. Sarcopenia is an age-related decrease in muscle mass and strength. We investigated the association between sarcopenia and incidence of pneumonia after endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) in patients aged ≥65 years.

pmc-13041488.title: Chlorine-coordinated iron single-atom nanozymes for amplified ferroptosis in triple-negative breast cancer therapy
pmc-13041488.creator: Mingming Yin, Bing-Hao Wang, Huijuan Wang, Jie Ouyang, Xingsheng Hu, Xiong Wang, Yongping Liu, Fenghua Xu, Yi Chen, Shuang-Feng Yin
pmc-13041488.description: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) represents an aggressive breast cancer subtype with limited therapeutic options and poor prognosis. Although single-atom nanozymes (SAzymes) show promise in cancer therapy, their ferroptosis-inducing capability remains limited. Herein, we present a rationally designed iron-based SAzyme with axial chlorine coordination (FeN4Cl) that integrates catalytic and metabolic functions to enhance ferroptosis in TNBC.

pmc-13403284.title: A novel triple-device recanalization strategy combining a small-diameter balloon, guide extension catheter, and distal protection device for large thrombus-induced coronary artery occlusion: a case report
pmc-13403284.creator: Yudai Tanaka, Riku Arai, Tetsuro Nagao, Keisuke Kojima, Yasuo Okumura
pmc-13403284.description: BackgroundLarge intracoronary thrombus during primary PCI for ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) remains challenging, particularly when aspiration techniques fail. We report a novel mechanical retrieval technique using balloon-assisted locking between a guide extension catheter and a distal protection device, enabling en bloc thrombus extraction.Case summaryAn 80-year-old man presented with inferior STEMI due to total occlusion of the proximal right coronary artery.

pmc-13448018.title: Multigene panel analysis of connective tissue and vascular genes in patients with a bleeding disorder of unknown cause or a cerebrovascular event
pmc-13448018.creator: Mona Florquin, Christine Van Laer, Cyrielle Kint, Chris Van Geet, Quentin Van Thillo, Kathleen Freson, Veerle Labarque
pmc-13448018.description: BackgroundBleeding disorder of unknown cause (BDUC) refers to patients with a significant bleeding phenotype despite normal hemostatic evaluation. Cerebrovascular events (CVEs) are neurologic deficits from intracerebral hemorrhages to hemorrhagic or ischemic strokes. A multigene panel for inherited connective tissue and vascular disorders (BLEED_panel) may improve diagnostic assessment.
